findings.description: The bucket is configured (per its own annotation) to be publicly accessible, and no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block or restrictive ACL/policy is present to prevent anonymous read/write access to its contents.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so objects are stored unencrypted, violating the requirement that encryption at rest be the default state for stored data.
No versioning block is configured, meaning accidental or malicious deletion/overwrite of objects in a bucket that is already publicly exposed cannot be recovered.
No logging block is configured, so there is no audit trail of access to this public, sensitive-data bucket.

A customer master data file (customer-master.xlsx) is uploaded into the aws_s3_bucket.data bucket, which is publicly accessible and unencrypted, exposing sensitive customer data to anyone with access to the bucket.
The object does not specify server_side_encryption and is stored in a bucket without default encryption, so the file is stored in plaintext.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined for a bucket holding financial data, leaving it stored unencrypted.
No versioning block is configured, allowing unrecoverable deletion or overwrite of financial records.
No logging block is present, preventing audit of access to sensitive financial data.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined, so operational data is stored unencrypted despite versioning being enabled.
No logging block is configured for this bucket, preventing audit of access.
Despite having versioning and logging configured, no server_side_encryption_configuration is present, so data science data is stored unencrypted.
